examples.en: In winter, sailfin sandfish tastes good grilled.
I bought a box of sailfin sandfish at the market.

examples.ko: 도루묵은 알이 톡톡 터지는 느낌이 재미있어요.
examples.en: The way the roe pops in sailfin sandfish is fun.
My grandmother made braised sailfin sandfish for me.
A lot of sailfin sandfish is caught off the coast of Gangwon Province.
I tried sailfin sandfish stew for the first time, and it tasted clean and light.

explain: 생선 이름이라서 주로 음식 이야기에서 나와요. 구이나 찌개로 먹고, '말짱 도루묵'이라는 비유 표현에도 들어가요.

phrases.example: 열심히 준비했는데 행사가 취소돼서 말짱 도루묵이 됐어요.
phrases.en: I prepared hard, but the event was canceled, so it was all for nothing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 애쓴 일이 아무 소용없이 처음 상태로 돌아갔을 때 아쉬움을 담아 말해요. 편한 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said with regret when effort ends up wasted and you are back where you started. It is casual.
phrases.en_equiv: all for nothing; back to square one

explain_en: It is a fish name, so it mostly comes up when talking about food. People grill it or put it in stew, and it also appears in the figurative expression '말짱 도루묵'.

examples.en: They drew water up from the well with a pulley.

examples.ko: 도르래를 쓰면 무거운 짐도 쉽게 들 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you use a pulley, you can lift even heavy loads easily.
We did a pulley experiment in science class.
The pulley is rusty, so it makes a strange noise.

examples.ko: 공사장에서는 도르래에 줄을 걸어 벽돌을 올려요.
examples.en: At the construction site, they hang a rope on a pulley to raise bricks.

examples.ko: 이 커튼은 도르래 줄을 당기면 열려요.
examples.en: This curtain opens when you pull the pulley cord.

explain: 과학 시간에 많이 나오는 말이고, 일상에서는 우물, 공사장, 블라인드 같은 이야기에서 만나요. 보통 '도르래를 달다', '도르래를 쓰다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It comes up in science class, and in daily life in talk about wells, construction sites and blinds. People usually say '도르래를 달다' (to attach a pulley) or '도르래를 쓰다' (to use a pulley).

examples.en: The old paper is curled up into a roll.
The marble rolled far away across the floor.

examples.ko: 얇은 김이 도르르 말려서 먹기 힘들어요.
examples.en: The thin seaweed sheet curls up, so it is hard to eat.

examples.ko: 아이가 이불을 도르르 말고 누워 있어요.
examples.en: The child is lying there rolled up in the blanket.
The toilet paper unrolled and piled up on the floor.

examples.ko: 동전이 책상 아래로 도르르 굴러 떨어졌어요.
examples.en: The coin rolled off and fell under the desk.

explain: 작고 가벼운 것이 굴러가거나 종이처럼 얇은 것이 말리는 모양에 써요. '데굴데굴'은 좀 더 크게 구르는 느낌이라 도르르와 느낌이 달라요. 주로 '도르르 말리다', '도르르 구르다'로 써요.
explain_en: It describes small, light things rolling along or thin things like paper curling up. '데굴데굴' feels bigger and heavier, so the feeling is different. It is mostly used as '도르르 말리다' or '도르르 구르다'.

examples.en: The baby shakes its head to say no.
I asked my friend for a favor, but all he did was shake his head.

examples.ko: 밥을 먹이면 아기가 도리질을 치며 입을 다물어요.
examples.en: When I try to feed the baby, it shakes its head and shuts its mouth.

examples.ko: 모두 찬성했는데 한 사람만 도리질을 했어요.
examples.en: Everyone agreed, but one person shook his head.

examples.ko: 도리질 한 번에 제 제안은 거절당했어요.
examples.en: With a single shake of the head, my suggestion was turned down.

examples.ko: 그는 아무 말 없이 도리질로 대답했어요.
examples.en: He answered with a shake of the head, without saying a word.

explain: 보통 '도리질을 하다/치다'로 쓰고, 싫다거나 아니라는 뜻으로 고개를 좌우로 흔드는 동작이에요. 어린아이의 모습을 말할 때 특히 잘 어울려요. 어른에게는 '고개를 젓다'가 더 일상적이에요.
explain_en: It is usually used as '도리질을 하다/치다' and means shaking your head side to side to say no. It fits especially well when describing small children. For adults, '고개를 젓다' is more everyday.

examples.en: The child shakes its head, saying it doesn't want to eat.
When I asked him, he shook his head without a word.

examples.ko: 동생은 안 간다며 계속 도리질하고 있어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling keeps shaking their head, saying they won't go.
Even when I asked, she shook her head and refused.
The way the baby shakes its head is so cute.
Even though my friend shook his head, I did not give up.

explain: '도리질을 하다'와 같은 뜻이고, 싫다·아니다·거절한다는 마음을 고개로 보여 줄 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '고개를 젓다'가 더 흔한 말투예요.
explain_en: It means the same as '도리질을 하다' and is used when you show refusal or disagreement with your head. In everyday talk, '고개를 젓다' is the more usual way to say it.

examples.en: Please cut the fish into three pieces.
The pencil is worn down, and only a short stub is left.

examples.ko: 찌개에 대파 한 도막을 넣으면 맛있어요.
examples.en: It tastes good if you put a piece of green onion in the stew.

examples.ko: 남은 나무 도막이 책상 밑에 떨어져 있어요.
examples.en: A leftover piece of wood is lying under the desk.

examples.ko: 빵 한 도막을 동생에게 나눠 줬어요.
examples.en: I shared a piece of bread with my younger sibling.

examples.ko: 긴 줄을 여러 도막으로 잘라서 썼어요.
examples.en: I cut the long rope into several pieces and used them.

explain: '토막'과 비슷하게 쓰는 말이에요. 생선, 나무, 줄처럼 길쭉한 것을 잘라 낸 한 덩이를 셀 때 '한 도막, 두 도막'이라고 말해요.
explain_en: It is used much like '토막'. You count long things cut into pieces, such as fish, wood or rope, as '한 도막, 두 도막'.

examples.en: My father runs a wholesale fruit business.

examples.ko: 도매업은 한 번에 많이 사고팔아서 값이 싸요.
examples.en: Wholesale deals in large amounts at a time, so prices are low.
My uncle worked in wholesale and then opened his own shop.
There are many wholesale merchants in this market.

examples.ko: 도매업이 어려워져서 문을 닫는 곳도 있어요.
examples.en: Wholesale has gotten harder, so some places are closing.
Do you know the difference between wholesale and retail?

explain: 반대말은 소비자에게 직접 파는 '소매업'이에요. 그 일을 하는 가게나 사람은 '도매상'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: The opposite is '소매업' (retail), which sells directly to consumers. A shop or person doing that work is also called a '도매상' (wholesaler).

examples.ko: 그 가수의 무대 의상은 꽤 도발적이에요.
examples.en: That singer's stage outfit is quite provocative.
He answered the provocative question calmly.
Many people say the ad is too provocative.
His way of speaking sounded provocative, and it upset me.

examples.ko: 이 그림은 색이 강하고 도발적이어서 눈에 띄어요.
examples.en: This painting has strong colors and is provocative, so it stands out.

examples.ko: 그의 태도는 도발적이지 않고 아주 부드러웠어요.
examples.en: His attitude was not provocative at all and was very gentle.

explain: '도발적이다', '도발적인 ~'처럼 써요. 말이나 행동에서는 상대를 자극해서 싸움을 거는 느낌이고, 패션이나 광고에서는 과감하고 시선을 끄는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is used as '도발적이다' or '도발적인 ~'. For words and actions it feels like provoking someone into a fight, while for fashion or ads it feels bold and attention-grabbing.

examples.ko: 새집에 도배장이를 불러서 벽지를 새로 발랐어요.
examples.en: We called a paperhanger to the new house and had the wallpaper redone.

examples.ko: 도배장이 아저씨가 하루 만에 방을 끝냈어요.
examples.en: The paperhanger finished the room in just one day.
My father worked as a paperhanger for a long time.
The paperhanger puts up wallpaper very straight.
Before moving, I got an estimate from a paperhanger.
The old house became clean thanks to the paperhanger's work.

explain: '도배'는 벽에 벽지를 바르는 일이고, 기술을 가진 사람 뒤에는 '-장이'를 붙여요(대장장이처럼). 사람 성격을 말할 때는 '-쟁이'(고집쟁이)라서 달라요. 직접 부를 때는 '아저씨', '사장님'처럼 높여 부르는 게 자연스러워요.
explain_en: '도배' is putting wallpaper on walls, and '-장이' is added to people with a craft skill (like 대장장이). For personality traits it is '-쟁이' (like 고집쟁이), so they are different. When addressing the person, polite terms like '아저씨' or '사장님' sound more natural.

examples.ko: 그 사람의 행동을 보니 어떤 속셈이 도사리고 있는 것 같아요.
examples.en: Judging by his behavior, it seems some hidden motive is lurking.

examples.ko: 아직도 세계 곳곳에는 평화를 위협하는 요인이 도사리고 있어요.
examples.en: Even now, factors that threaten peace are lurking all over the world.

examples.ko: 산길 곳곳에 위험이 도사려서 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: Danger lurks all along the mountain path, so you have to be careful.

examples.ko: 친절한 미소 뒤에 도사린 속셈을 알아챘어요.
examples.en: I noticed the hidden motive lurking behind the friendly smile.

examples.ko: 어두운 골목에는 위험이 도사릴 수 있어요.
examples.en: Danger can lurk in dark alleys.
Anxiety always lurks somewhere in my mind.

explain: 위험, 불안, 속셈처럼 좋지 않은 것이 겉으로는 안 보이게 숨어 있을 때 '~이/가 도사리고 있다'로 말해요. 그냥 '숨어 있다'보다 곧 나타날 것 같은 위협 느낌이 있어요. '도사리고 앉다'처럼 자리 잡고 앉는 뜻도 있어요.
explain_en: When something bad such as danger, anxiety or a hidden motive is out of sight, you say '~이/가 도사리고 있다'. Compared with plain '숨어 있다', it feels like a threat that might appear soon. It also has a sense of settling into a seat, as in '도사리고 앉다'.

examples.ko: 그의 설명은 너무 도식적이라서 와닿지 않아요.
examples.en: His explanation is too formulaic, so it doesn't resonate with me.

examples.ko: 도식적인 이야기보다 새로운 줄거리가 보고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to see a fresh plot rather than a formulaic story.

examples.ko: 이 드라마는 선과 악을 도식적으로 나눠요.
examples.en: This drama divides good and evil in a formulaic way.
I tried to find an answer that was not formulaic.
The presentation was formulaic, so it was a bit boring.

examples.ko: 도식적 사고를 버리고 자유롭게 생각해 보세요.
examples.en: Drop formulaic thinking and try to think freely.

explain: 정해진 틀에 단순하게 끼워 맞춘 느낌을 말해서 대체로 부정적인 평가예요. 영화, 소설, 설명, 생각을 비평할 때 '도식적이다', '도식적인 ~'로 써요.
explain_en: It describes something forced into a fixed, simple pattern, so it is usually a negative judgment. You use '도식적이다' or '도식적인 ~' when criticizing films, novels, explanations or ways of thinking.

examples.en: I explained the complicated content by laying it out in a chart.

examples.ko: 이 과정을 한눈에 보이게 도식화해 보세요.
examples.en: Try to diagram this process so it can be seen at a glance.
The teacher laid out the grammar rules in a diagram.
If you put your thoughts into a diagram, it is easy to organize them.
An attitude that tries to reduce every problem to a diagram is risky.

examples.ko: 발표 자료에서 순서를 도식화한 부분이 좋았어요.
examples.en: I liked the part of the slides where the order was shown in a diagram.

explain: '정리하다'와 달리 그림, 표, 도표로 보이게 만든다는 느낌이 강해요. 복잡한 것을 단순한 틀로 줄여 버린다는 부정적인 뉘앙스로 쓰일 때도 있어요.
explain_en: Unlike '정리하다', it strongly suggests turning something into a picture, table or chart. Sometimes it has a negative nuance of squeezing something complex into a simple frame.

examples.ko: 학생들이 길 양쪽에 도열해서 손님을 맞았어요.
examples.en: Students lined up on both sides of the road to welcome the guests.
The president walked past the soldiers standing in formation.
The players are lined up at the entrance of the stadium.
The staff lined up at the entrance and waited for the boss.
Fans were lined up at the airport exit.
The graduates lined up side by side on the field.

explain: 행사에서 환영하거나 맞이하려고 사람들이 질서 있게 늘어서는 모습에 써요. 차례를 기다리며 서는 '줄을 서다'와는 달라요. 글이나 뉴스 느낌이 나서 일상 대화에서는 '나란히 서다'로도 말해요.
explain_en: It describes people standing in an orderly row to welcome someone at an event. It differs from '줄을 서다', which is waiting your turn. It sounds like writing or news, so in daily talk people also say '나란히 서다'.

examples.en: I go to learn pottery every weekend.
I made a cup myself in pottery class.
I became interested in pottery, so I signed up at a workshop.

examples.ko: 이 도예 작품은 색이 정말 독특해요.
examples.en: The color of this pottery piece is really unique.

examples.ko: 도예로 만든 그릇은 하나하나 모양이 달라요.
examples.en: Each bowl made by pottery has a different shape.
My friend gave me a pottery experience class as a gift.

explain: 만든 물건은 '도자기', 만드는 일이나 분야는 '도예'라고 해요. '도예 수업', '도예 공방', '도예 체험'처럼 뒤에 말이 붙는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: The finished item is '도자기' (ceramic ware), while the craft or field of making it is '도예'. It is often followed by another word, as in '도예 수업', '도예 공방' and '도예 체험'.

examples.ko: 그 도예가의 작품은 해외에서도 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: That potter's works are popular overseas too.

examples.ko: 저는 도예가가 되고 싶어서 대학에 진학했어요.
examples.en: I wanted to become a potter, so I went on to college.
I met a famous potter and listened to his story.

examples.ko: 저는 그 도예가의 제자가 되려고 지방으로 내려갔어요.
examples.en: I moved out to the countryside to become that potter's apprentice.

examples.ko: 도예가는 하루 종일 흙을 만지며 일해요.
examples.en: A potter works all day long, handling clay.
My aunt, who is a potter, gave me a cup as a gift.

explain: '-가'가 붙어서 전문가나 작가의 느낌이 있어요. '도공'도 비슷하지만 도예가는 작품을 만드는 예술가 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: The suffix '-가' gives it the feel of a specialist or artist. '도공' is similar, but 도예가 sounds more like an artist who creates works.

examples.en: If you ignore reality and only chase dreams, life gets hard.

examples.ko: 회사가 직원들의 의견을 도외시해서 불만이 커졌어요.
examples.en: The company disregarded the employees' opinions, so complaints grew.

examples.ko: 건강을 도외시한 채 일만 하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't just work while ignoring your health.
We can't disregard that problem.

examples.ko: 정부는 지방의 어려움을 도외시하지 않겠다고 했어요.
examples.en: The government said it would not overlook the difficulties of the regions.
If you neglect the basics, your skills won't improve.

explain: '무시하다'와 비슷하지만 일부러 깔보기보다 관심을 두지 않고 문제 삼지 않는다는 느낌이에요. '~을/를 도외시하다' 꼴로 쓰고, 말보다는 글이나 뉴스에 어울려요. 반대로 중요하게 여기면 '중시하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is close to '무시하다', but it feels more like not paying attention or not taking something up than deliberately looking down on it. It is used as '~을/를 도외시하다' and suits writing and news more than speech. The opposite, treating something as important, is '중시하다'.

examples.en: Gyeongju was the capital of Silla.
The capital of Joseon is today's Seoul.

examples.ko: 왕은 새로운 도읍지를 찾으려고 신하들을 보냈어요.
examples.en: The king sent his officials to find a new capital.

examples.ko: 이 유적은 옛 백제의 도읍지에 있어요.
examples.en: These ruins are in the old capital of Baekje.
As the capital changed, the look of the city changed too.
I took a trip to Buyeo, which is famous as a former capital.

explain: 옛 나라의 수도를 말할 때 쓰고, 역사 이야기에서 자주 만나요. 지금의 나라 수도는 보통 '수도'라고 해요.
explain_en: It refers to the capital of an old kingdom and shows up in talk about history. For the capital of a country today, people usually say '수도'.

examples.en: He was hungry, so he stole some bread.
You must not steal other people's things.
The person caught stealing shed tears.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 도적질한 일을 지금도 후회해요.
examples.en: I still regret stealing something when I was little.
Old tales have people who live by stealing.

examples.ko: 도적질해서 번 돈으로 사는 건 옳지 않아요.
examples.en: Living on money earned by stealing is not right.

explain: '도둑질하다'와 거의 같은 말이고, '훔치다'보다 좀 더 나쁜 짓이라고 꾸짖는 느낌이 있어요. 옛이야기나 교훈 같은 말투에 잘 어울려요. 남의 아이디어를 몰래 쓰는 것에도 비유로 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is almost the same as '도둑질하다', and compared with '훔치다' it carries a stronger tone of scolding the act as wrong. It fits old tales and moral-lesson speech. It can also be used figuratively for secretly taking someone's ideas.

examples.ko: 감기가 다 나은 줄 알았는데 다시 도졌어요.
examples.en: I thought my cold was fully gone, but it flared up again.
When the weather gets cold, my knee pain flares up.
My back problem flared up, so I went to the hospital.

examples.ko: 비가 오면 오래된 상처가 도지곤 해요.
examples.en: When it rains, my old injury tends to act up.
Be careful so that your allergy doesn't flare up.

examples.ko: 병이 도질까 봐 약을 계속 먹고 있어요.
examples.en: I keep taking my medicine in case the illness flares up again.

explain: 나았던 병이 다시 심해질 때, 또는 나쁜 버릇이 다시 나올 때 써요. '악화되다'와 달리 '다시'라는 느낌이 있고, '재발하다'와 비슷해요. 활용은 '도져요', '도졌어요'로 해요.
explain_en: It is used when an illness that had gotten better becomes worse again, or when a bad habit comes back. Unlike '악화되다', it carries the sense of 'again', and it is close to '재발하다'. It conjugates as '도져요' and '도졌어요'.

examples.ko: 그는 자기 노래에 도취해서 눈을 감고 불렀어요.
examples.en: He was so absorbed in his own singing that he sang with his eyes closed.
The players, drunk with victory, shouted out loud.

examples.ko: 음악에 도취하면 시간 가는 줄 몰라요.
examples.en: When I get lost in music, I lose track of time.
Don't be too wrapped up in yourself.

examples.ko: 아름다운 경치에 도취해 한참 서 있었어요.
examples.en: I was so enchanted by the beautiful scenery that I stood there for a while.
I got carried away by the praise and made a big mistake.

explain: '~에 도취하다'로 쓰고, 좋은 것에 푹 빠져서 정신을 못 차리는 느낌이에요. 자기 자신이나 성공에 도취하면 부정적이고, 음악이나 경치에 도취하면 긍정적일 수 있어요. '빠지다'보다 격식 있는 글말 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is used as '~에 도취하다' and feels like being so absorbed in something good that you lose your head. Being intoxicated with yourself or success is negative, while being enchanted by music or scenery can be positive. It sounds more formal and written than '빠지다'.

examples.en: That actor has a sophisticated, city-like image.
This cafe has an urbane, stylish atmosphere.
Her outfit is urbane, so it stands out.
Even though he is from the countryside, his way of speaking is urbane.
The room decorated in an urbane style is very neat.
It is a design that stands out for its urbane sense.

explain: 사람, 옷차림, 분위기가 세련되고 도시 사람 같을 때 칭찬하는 느낌으로 써요. '도시적'과 비슷하지만 도회적은 세련된 이미지가 더 강해요. 반대 느낌은 '소박하다', '시골스럽다'예요.
explain_en: It is used with a complimentary feel for a person, outfit or atmosphere that looks refined and like a city dweller. It is close to '도시적', but 도회적 has a stronger image of sophistication. The opposite feeling is '소박하다' or '시골스럽다'.
